sections.title: The Meeting
sections.content:
Michael Kudlick of SRI-ARC announces a meeting at SRI-ARC on the Network Mail problem raised at the January 1973 Principal Investigators' Meeting in San Diego. It is set for Thursday, February 22, 1973, at 8:30 AM in the SRI-ARC conference room, with Friday as a second day if needed.

The agenda covers the problem and alternate solutions. The goal is a clear definition of the solution, the steps to take, and who should do what. Results will be published as an RFC, as is done with other suggested protocols.
sections.eli5: A date and place are set for people to meet and plan how to send mail between computers.

sections.title: Aspects of the Problem
sections.content:
Several subsystems on the Network already send and receive mail. The principal problem is to coordinate and extend them so that:

  • uniform user and site identifications are used;
  • the File Transfer Protocol lets mail be originated and distributed anywhere without a central system;
  • a sender can record the dialogue and have it catalogued for others to read;
  • there is a way to handle mail for TIP users.

SRI-ARC has been looking at using the File Transfer Protocol to deliver NIC Journal mail without the user needing NLS, and intends to integrate this with Tenex SNDMSG. It wants questions of identification, recorded dialogue and coordination settled at the design level before implementation proceeds.
sections.eli5: Everyone needs the same kind of name tag, a way to send mail directly, and a way to keep a record if they want one.

sections.title: Role of the NIC and Logistics
sections.content:
The meeting will consider whether the Network Information Center (NIC) should offer services in related areas:

  • maintaining identification files for all network users and sites;
  • recording and cataloguing in the NIC Journal mail the sender wants kept;
  • distributing Journal or message mail using the File Transfer Protocol on request;
  • providing dialogue group identifications, so items can be sent to several people with a common interest.

Anyone wishing to attend should notify Mil Jernigan at SRI-ARC, who can also arrange motel reservations.
sections.eli5: The library of the network might keep the address book and a record of messages, and help send them to groups.
